# Learning what a correct past response reveals about this learner

Use the existing EdNet development learners and unchanged before-bundle forecasts. A correct answer on an easy exercise reveals less about the learner than a correct answer on a hard one. Test whether a finite-grid Rasch ability update from the last sixteen eligible responses improves next-answer log loss. A response to an unseen question falls back to its skill estimate. Estimate item difficulty from training learners only, with five user-disjoint folds for training features. The fold is the existing training bucket modulo five. Estimate average correctness hierarchically, shrinking the primary skill toward overall training success with 30 pseudo-observations and each question toward its skill with 6 pseudo-observations. Use the fixed grid −3 to 3 in increments of .25, a unit normal prior and a logistic item-response curve. Integrate the current item's probability of success against the posterior after the past responses. This is a finite-history empirical Bayes score, using marginal item performance in the role of a difficulty estimate.

Carry forward published simpleKT (item-aware and skill-only), SAKT, the prior development tree/blend family and the clock-only model. Add same-budget tree controls with current question/skill difficulty and support alone, then previous-question mean difficulty and observed accuracy over the same sixteen answers. Compare with a tree also receiving the finite-grid forecast, posterior mean and variance. Include the mechanistic forecast in isolation. Every new tree uses 350 GPU CatBoost iterations, depth 6, learning rate .1, seed 732 and the existing clock and history inputs. All fitting uses buckets 0–59. Score buckets 70–79 only. This fixed design uses no tuning labels. Screen for gains exceeding .015 nats against every control and a positive simultaneous lower bound under 5,000 paired learner resamples. Break down residuals by current-question support and presence of training overlap, report all rows and do not test previously reserved learners.
